## Objective
- Build a complete, playable rhythm game using local music files or YouTube videos with automatic synchronization.

## Requirements
- Support local audio upload.
- Support YouTube video links.
- Provide an auto-synchronized rhythm chart.
- Offer playable keyboard and touch controls.
- Include visible scoring, accuracy, combo, rank, pause, restart, and fullscreen controls.

## Decisions
- Built a four-lane, neon pulse aesthetic.
- Used Web Audio onset analysis for uploaded files and a BPM grid fallback.
- Used the YouTube IFrame API for YouTube playback.
- Assumed desktop and mobile responsiveness are both required.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the main application structure in `index.html`.
- Created responsive visual styling in `styles.css`.
- Implemented gameplay, audio analysis, chart generation, demo mode, YouTube controls, scoring, and touch/keyboard inputs in `app.js`.
- Started a local server on port 3002.
- Verified the page loads with no application console errors.

### Active
- Final browser gameplay polish and verification.

### Blocked
- No functional blockers remain.

## Next Move
1. Perform an end-to-end demo run and verify note timing and scoring.
2. Test local audio upload with a real file.
3. Test YouTube loading and playback in a browser where embedding is allowed.
4. Verify mobile viewport layout and touch controls.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Page structure and UI.
- `styles.css`: Full responsive visual design.
- `app.js`: Game logic, audio analysis, chart sync, and playback.

## Important Context
- The local server is running on `http://localhost:3002`.
- The initial implementation includes a built-in “THE PULSE” demo track.
- YouTube use relies on browser embedding and regional/content restrictions.

## Objective
- Complete and polish the existing playable rhythm game, including the newly requested long-note feature.

## Requirements
- Support local audio upload and YouTube links, auto-synchronized charts, keyboard/touch controls, scoring, pause, restart, and fullscreen.
- Add long notes (“롱노트 추가”).

## Decisions
- Four-lane neon rhythm game; local audio uses Web Audio analysis with a BPM-grid fallback, while YouTube uses a user-adjustable BPM grid.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, gameplay, chart generation, audio analysis, demo mode, YouTube embedding, scoring, and controls.
- Verified demo gameplay and local WAV upload/chart generation in headless Chromium; desktop/mobile screenshots captured.

### Active
- Long-note implementation has started: `app.js` now declares `heldLanes` as a `Set`, but no long-note charting, rendering, input-hold, or scoring behavior has been implemented or verified.

### Blocked
- YouTube test video loaded but playback returned `VIDEO UNAVAILABLE`; likely depends on embed permissions or browser/network restrictions.

## Next Move
1. Implement long-note chart data, rendering, hold/release input handling for keyboard and touch, and appropriate scoring/miss behavior in `app.js`.
2. Add or adjust any UI/help text needed to explain long notes.
3. Run syntax checks and browser gameplay verification, including long-note hold/release and existing demo/local-audio flows.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic; long-note work is pending here.
- `index.html`: Game structure and help text.
- `styles.css`: Responsive visual styling.

## Important Context
- Local server was running at `http://localhost:3002` during prior verification.
- Existing verification screenshots: `/tmp/opencode/pulsewave-desktop.png` and `/tmp/opencode/pulsewave-mobile.png`.
- The latest change to `app.js` is uncommitted; project files were untracked in the prior `git status`.
